bull_bear.body:
- 35 years of operating experience in pharmaceuticals
- Global reach with presence across 50+ countries and export-led revenue (70% of revenue from exports)
- Regulatory approvals/registrations from multiple international health authorities (e.g. NAFDAC Nigeria, PPB Kenya, FMHACA Ethiopia, Rwanda FDA) supporting market access breadth
- Advanced technology and automation at the new Pen facility, including AI-enabled quality systems and a Digital Manufacturing Execution System (MES) with real-time monitoring and data integrity
- In-house R&D and innovation pipeline developing differentiated formulations and optimising manufacturing processes
- Facilities designed and built to meet EU GMP and USFDA standards, supporting regulated-market access
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export revenue concentration — A significant contribution of exports to Company revenue exposes it to foreign exchange fluctuations, geopolitical developments, changing trade regulations and evolving statutory compliance requirements across multiple territories.
- Foreign exchange volatility — Explicitly flagged as a business risk given the scale of export operations; adverse currency movements can affect realisations and margins.
- Regulatory and compliance risk across jurisdictions — The pharmaceutical industry operates in a dynamic, highly regulated environment; changes in domestic and international regulatory frameworks and evolving statutory compliance requirements across multiple countries where the Company holds approvals/registrations could affect operations.
- Supply chain disruption — Flagged as a key risk area; the Company mitigates through business continuity planning and supplier diversification but disruption to inputs or logistics could impact production continuity.
- Raw material price volatility — Fluctuations in raw material prices are cited as a risk that can affect cost of production and margins.
- Pricing pressure — Cited among key risks facing the pharmaceutical business, particularly relevant given cost-competitive dynamics in generics/formulations markets.
- Cybersecurity threats — Explicitly listed among the Company's key operational/regulatory risk concerns in the Risk and Concerns section.
- Credit and liquidity risk — Contractual and legal disputes, credit risk and liquidity risk are named as business risks the Company is exposed to, particularly in connection with its export-heavy revenue base.

business.body: Kilitch Drugs (India) Limited is a pharmaceutical manufacturer with facilities in India (Mumbai and the new Pen, Maharashtra greenfield plant) and Ethiopia (via subsidiary Kilitch Estro Biotech PLC), spanning sterile injectables (vials, ampoules, lyophilized), ophthalmic preparations and nutraceutical/effervescent products across multiple therapeutic areas. The company is organised as a single reportable segment (pharmaceutical business under Ind AS 108) and derives 70% of revenue from exports across 50+ countries, holding regulatory approvals/registrations from health authorities in the Philippines, Cambodia, Sudan, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Zambia, Rwanda, Ethiopia and Yemen among others.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Sterile Injectables:** Vials, Ampoules, Lyophilized injectables
- **Nutraceuticals & Effervescent:** Tablets, Powder, Effervescent formulations
- **Ophthalmic:** Ophthalmic preparations

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Investing in the new Pen, Maharashtra greenfield facility, with advanced manufacturing technologies, AI-enabled quality systems and digitally integrated production, to strengthen manufacturing capabilities and supply chain resilience.
- Operating the Mumbai facility as the manufacturing backbone, complemented by the new Pen facility, to provide operational flexibility and uninterrupted supply.
- Expanding the global footprint through the Ethiopia manufacturing facility, supporting a long-term international expansion strategy across Africa.
- Driving growth through the in-house Research & Development Centre, developing differentiated formulations, improving existing products and optimising manufacturing processes.
- Pursuing expansion into regulated international markets alongside continued technology investment.
- Strengthening international presence through new product registrations and approvals in strategic export markets, including French West Africa and the Philippines.
- Maintaining a diversified, internationally-footprinted business (Asia, Africa, the CIS region and Latin America) tailored to region-specific regulatory requirements to expand market share.
- The Board's stated philosophy is to conserve resources for further growth of the Company: it retained the entire FY2025-26 profit in the profit and loss account (no transfer to general reserve) and did not recommend a dividend, prioritising reinvestment over shareholder payout. There are no associate or joint venture companies; the Company has no material unlisted Indian subsidiary.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company completed a new greenfield manufacturing facility at Pen, Maharashtra during FY2025-26, designed with advanced manufacturing technologies, AI-enabled quality systems and digitally integrated production processes to meet WHO, EU-GMP and USFDA standards; the facility spans a 14+ acre campus with 18,000+ sq. mtr. built-up area, covering sterile injectable manufacturing (vials, ampoules, lyophilized), nutraceuticals & effervescent (tablets, powder) and ophthalmic preparations, plus integrated QC & microbiology laboratories and an automated-handling warehouse. Operations at Pen are set to commence in phases in FY2026-27, complementing the existing Mumbai facility which remains the manufacturing backbone. Separately, the Ethiopia manufacturing facility (via subsidiary Kilitch Estro Biotech PLC) continues to expand the Company's African footprint and achieved more than 100% revenue growth during FY2025-26 as part of the long-term international expansion strategy.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global economy expected to grow 3.1% in CY2026 (down from 3.4% in CY2025), with risks from geopolitical conflicts, energy disruption and trade uncertainty.
- IMF projects India's GDP to grow 6.4% in both FY2025-26 and FY2026-27, significantly outpacing global growth of approximately 3.0%, underpinning a strong macro backdrop for the Indian pharmaceutical industry.
- Growth drivers for the global pharmaceutical industry include increasing healthcare expenditure, ageing populations, rising chronic disease prevalence, expanding healthcare access and advances in biotechnology, biologics and precision medicine.
- Manufacturers with diversified product portfolios, strong regulatory compliance, advanced manufacturing capabilities and broad international presence are expected to be best positioned to benefit from expanding global healthcare demand.
- Rising chronic/lifestyle disease burden, ageing populations, demand for affordable generics, expanding universal healthcare coverage in emerging economies and growing preventive-healthcare preference are driving sustained demand for injectable, ophthalmic, oral solid, liquid and nutraceutical formulations.
- Global pharmaceutical companies are increasingly outsourcing manufacturing to cost-efficient, quality-compliant partners to optimise supply chains and accelerate market access.
- India is strengthening its position as a leading pharmaceutical manufacturing and export hub, aided by cost-competitive manufacturing, a skilled scientific workforce, a strong regulatory ecosystem, the PLI Scheme, promotion of bulk drug manufacturing and the 'Make in India' focus.
- The India pharmaceutical market grew 10% in FY26, with the chronic segment growing 14% versus 7% for the acute segment (IQVIA MAT March 2026 data).
- Company is supported by long-standing customer relationships, a diversified geographical presence and a robust product pipeline to expand market share.
- Company describes a 'robust product pipeline' and cites new product registrations/approvals secured during the year in strategic export markets (French West Africa and the Philippines) as support for continued international expansion, though no quantified order-book figures are disclosed.
